This appears to be a CBP ruling on a syringe-type cartridge for a 3D printer. The question is whether it falls under 9018.31 (syringes, with or without needles, used in medical sciences) or under parts of 3D printers (8485) or plastic articles (3926.90).

The ruling states "We note that this cartridge is a graduated syringe", yet it is not for medical use. Heading 9018 covers instruments used in medical, surgical, dental or veterinary sciences. A non-medical syringe would not belong there. Heading 8485 covers machines for additive manufacturing, and 8485.90 covers their parts. The cartridge is a reservoir part of a 3D printer. Under Section XVI notes, parts of plastic are not excluded, since Section XVI note 1 excludes only certain items, and 3926 is not among them. So the item is a part of an additive manufacturing machine under 8485.90.

The subheading structure is 8485.90.00 with the 10-digit statistical suffix 8485.90.0000. I'm going with that.

I considered 3926.90.9990 as the alternative, but a part suitable for use solely with a 3D printer goes to 8485.90.

{"hts_code": "8485.90.0000", "reason": "The plastic syringe-style cartridge is not for medical use (so not heading 9018) and is a reservoir/dispensing part solely used in an additive-manufacturing machine, so it is classified as a part of such machines in heading 8485."}
